run.runNote: Phase 1 Step 1-2 (source exploration + candidate extraction query generation only; no CodeQL execution, no compile, no LLM labeling in this round) against the dfetch_vuln source tree. WORKFLOW.md confirms Pass 1 = CWE-022/023/036/073 Path Traversal with pass query name Pass1_PathTraversal.ql. The CodeQL database dfetch-db sits INSIDE the source tree, so all exploration, file traversal, and evidence collection excluded dfetch-db (only codeql-database.yml and the src.zip listing were read for metadata/scope). The database sourceLocationPrefix matches the explored tree (creation sha 81020d54), so file/line evidence below refers to the same snapshot the database was built from. The audit target is the dfetch tool itself (version 0.5.1), a manifest-driven dependency-fetching CLI: it reads a YAML manifest (dfetch.yaml) describing external git/svn projects, fetches them and places them at manifest-specified destinations, applies manifest-specified patches, and writes metadata files. There is NO web surface: all attacker-relevant boundaries are file content (the manifest, fetched-project metadata, patch files, .gitmodules) and subprocess output (git/svn remote-repository data), plus the operator-level CLI.

target.projectDescription: dfetch 0.5.1 (dfetch/__init__.py __version__) - a Python CLI tool ('Dependency Fetch') for vendoring external git/svn dependencies described by a dfetch.yaml manifest. Core flow: dfetch/__main__.py builds an argparse parser from 9 subcommands (check/diff/environment/freeze/import/init/report/update/validate) and runs sys.argv through it; dfetch.manifest.manifest.find_manifest()/get_manifest() walk the CWD tree for dfetch.yaml, validate it against a pykwalify schema (dfetch/resources/schema.yaml) and yaml.safe_load it into Manifest/ProjectEntry/Remote objects (fields: name, dst, src, patch, url, repo-path, branch, tag, revision, vcs, remote); dfetch.project.make() wraps each ProjectEntry in GitRepo/SvnRepo (dfetch/project/git.py, svn.py, both subclass dfetch/project/vcs.py VCS); VCS.update() deletes the existing destination (safe_rm), fetches (git: pathlib.Path(local_path).mkdir + GitLocalRepo.checkout_version with in_directory chdir, sparse-checkout file write, os.listdir/shutil.move/safe_rmtree of the manifest 'src' subtree; svn: SvnRepo._export -> 'svn export --force <url> <dst>' subprocess with manifest dst), applies the manifest 'patch' file via patch_ng (fromfile + patch_set.apply(root=local_path)), hashes the destination tree (os.walk + open + read) and dumps .dfetch_data.yaml metadata (Metadata.dump, open(self.path)) where the path is built from the manifest destination. 'dfetch import' derives ProjectEntry dst/src from git submodule/.gitmodules or svn:externals subprocess output (dfetch/vcs/git.py submodules(), dfetch/project/svn.py externals()). 'dfetch diff' writes '<project-name>.patch' (name from the manifest) via open(patch_name, 'w'). 'dfetch report' globs the destination CWD and calls infer_license.api.guess_file; sbom reporter writes via cyclonedx outputter.output_to_file(outfile) with the CLI --outfile.

guardsAndEvidence.evidence: dfetch/manifest/validate.py:11-27 validates every manifest (get_manifest manifest.py:254, get_childmanifests manifest.py:276) against dfetch/resources/schema.yaml: 'dst' is type str + unique, 'patch' is type str, 'vcs' is enum git/svn, 'src' is type ANY - the schema contains NO path-content constraint (no '..' rejection, no absolute-path check, no charset/pattern restriction), so traversal values in dst/src/patch PASS validation; validation is structure-only, not a path sanitizer

svn.py:227-236 _parse_file_pattern raises RuntimeError when 'src' contains more than one '*' (only for the svn path) - the ONLY observed content restriction on 'src'; it does not block '..', absolute paths or mixed separators
project/git.py:84-92 _determine_what_to_fetch rejects shortened git SHA revisions; svn.py:181-182 rejects non-numeric svn revisions - these validate version fields, not path fields

no startswith/anchor/realpath-containment/'..' check exists anywhere on dst, src or patch: os.path.realpath is used only for normalization (manifest.py:247/:270, metadata.py:129/:132) and one equality comparison (import_.py:195); pathlib .relative_to appears once (manifest.py:274) for a log prefix, not as a base-containment guard on destinations; basename appears once (metadata.py:131) for sibling-filename construction

update.py:70-77: the fetch runs with CWD = manifest directory and child-manifest discovery with CWD = project.destination (os.chdir util.py:52) - relative dst values resolve under these roots, but an absolute or '..'-containing dst escapes the scoping entirely (chdir does not confine subsequent relative resolution of an absolute path)

guardsAndEvidence.note: vcs.py:103-105: os.path.exists(local_path) check then safe_rm(local_path) then _fetch_impl then Metadata.dump (vcs.py:129-130) - the exists-check/delete/recreate/metadata-write sequence has classic TOCTOU shape; also vcs.py:117 os.path.exists(patch) then vcs.py:134 fromfile(patch). TOCTOU is not separately extractable as a candidate row - recorded as evidence.

update.py:75-77 and check.py:69-71: after fetching, dfetch chdirs into project.destination (the manifest dst) and re-reads any dfetch.yaml found there via get_childmanifests (manifest.py:263-280, os.walk-based find_file from '.') - fetched REMOTE content supplies the next round of dst/src/patch values (used only for recommendations, not auto-fetch, in this version - recommendations are logged, not fetched: common.py:42-70)

vcs/git.py:144 'git remote add origin {remote}' / :156 'git fetch --depth 1 origin {version}' and svn.py:113/:139/:252/:268 f-string commands interpolate manifest-controlled url/src/tag values into shell-less subprocess.run argument lists (cmdline.py:48-55 splits strings on spaces); this is Pass 2 command/argument-injection material - recorded here for labeling context, NOT emitted as Pass 1 sink rows

svn.py:70 normalizes os.sep to '/' for the imported external dst; vcs/git.py:169 builds 'src + "/" + file_to_copy' with a hardcoded forward slash; on Windows pathlib/os.path treat both '/' and '\' as separators, so manifest values with either separator traverse identically; no separator normalization guard exists for dst

matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, os/shutil/yaml/args name conventions). Member-name matching (.mkdir/.apply/.relative_to) is receiver-name-agnostic on purpose: receiver identity cannot be proven syntactically (a name collision would be a false candidate row - none observed on these paths in this snapshot; receiver hints like self.local_path/src/patch_set are emitted for the labeling step).

uncoveredCases: String-concatenation / f-string path building is NOT emitted as rows: vcs/git.py:169 'src + "/" + file_to_copy', vcs/git.py:270 'toplevel + "/.gitmodules"', diff.py:166 patch_name = f"{project.name}.patch", metadata.py:131 f"{BASENAME}-{os.path.basename(self._destination)}.{EXT}" - BinaryExpr plus and f-string JoinedStr nodes are indistinguishable from ordinary string building at AST level without type resolution; the consuming sink rows (shutil.move/open/run_on_cmdline/realpath) anchor these channels instead.

git-side subprocess file writes (git init/fetch/reset --hard inside in_directory(local_path), vcs/git.py:142-157) are NOT emitted as Pass 1 sink rows: the file writes are performed by the git process with CWD set by the in_directory chdir channel (util.py:52, emitted); the git command strings are Pass 2 (command/argument injection) material. The svn-side export IS emitted (svn.py:243-246) because it passes the destination path explicitly as a Python-constructed argument list element.

run_on_cmdline positional structure: in SvnRepo._export the dst is the LAST element of a concatenated list expression (['svn','export','--force'] + rev.split(' ') + [url, dst]) whose length varies with the revision argument - the row therefore reports arg_index -1 with the dst position documented in the query comments rather than a fixed index.

patch_set.apply(0, root=self.local_path, fuzz=True) passes the destination root as a KEYWORD argument (vcs.py:138) - no positional index exists; the row reports arg_index -1 with the root= keyword documented. The patch-internal target paths that patch_ng writes are parsed inside the patch_ng library (not part of this database) - the apply row anchors the channel, the written paths are invisible to this extraction.

Dynamic dispatch ambiguity: .mkdir/.apply/.relative_to/.stdout matching is name-based; a non-path/non-process receiver with the same member name would produce a false candidate row (no such collisions observed in this snapshot; receiver hints self.local_path/patch_set/result are emitted for labeling).

args.<field> CLI reads are matched by the syntactic receiver name 'args' in dfetch/commands/*.py and dfetch/__main__.py - a differently-named Namespace variable would be missed (not observed; every command uses 'args'). args.func (dispatch callback, __main__.py:67) is explicitly excluded; commands taking an unused '_' parameter (import/environment/validate) produce no param rows by design.

The manifest schema's dst-uniqueness and vcs-enum constraints (dfetch/resources/schema.yaml) are enforcement evidence, not extractable AST nodes - recorded in guardsAndEvidence instead of candidate rows.

Metadata.path / VCS.local_path / ProjectEntry.destination property definitions are the internal propagation backbone of the manifest-to-filesystem pipeline but are property getters, not calls; the kwargs.get source rows and the file_api_def sink rows bracket them, and the property chains themselves are left to the LLM labeling/summary step (MySummaries material).
